newsitem.title: USA: TWA sees possibility of Q3 profit.
newsitem.headline: TWA sees possibility of Q3 profit.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc, which reported a greater-than-expected second-quarter net loss on Wednesday, said Thursday it tentatively expected it would post a profit in the third quarter.
TWA spokesman Mark Abels confirmed published comments attributed to Chief Financial Officer Michael Palumbo, who said the company was "cautiously optimistic" for a third-quarter profit.

The carrier, which has been reeling from the effects of Flight 800's crash a little over one year ago, reported a net loss of $15.9 million for the second quarter, or $0.36 per share. It was the only major U.S. carrier to post a loss for the June quarter.
On Tuesday, the St. Louis-based airline announced it would cut 1,000 jobs, or about four percent of its workforce.
First Call analysts' estimates currently project third-quarter profit of $0.26 per share.
